lead.hed: U.S. and Indian soldiers compared aviation procedures in the Rajasthan desert
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted Wednesday: Spc. Rashone Dempsey of the 11th Airborne Division listened as Indian Army aviation personnel walked through aircraft capabilities during exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026 at Mahajan Field Firing Range. The photo was taken Sept. 22 and posted Sept. 23. Partner exchange, not a deployment order.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Army National Guard photo by Staff Sgt. Kalina Hyche · DVIDS 9959760 · Public domain · Spc. Rashone Dempsey listens as Indian Army aviation personnel discuss aircraft capabilities, Mahajan Field Firing Range, Rajasthan, India, Sept. 22, 2026.

political.hed: A Spanish paper says the CIA warned Europe of drones launched from ships
political.insight: Defense News, Thursday, citing El Mundo: an anonymous Lithuanian intelligence source said the CIA assessed that Spain, France, or Italy could be targeted by Gerbera-type drones launched from commercial vessels in the Mediterranean. Defense News says the report has not been independently corroborated. Warning claim, not a confirmed attack.

political.hed: Heritage draws five drone lessons from Ukraine for NATO's northeastern flank
political.insight: Heritage Foundation, Tuesday: a defense report argues Ukrainian forces have used drones as sensors, munitions, and platforms to offset a larger military, and that NATO's northeastern flank should study those lessons. Report, not a new U.S. order.

political.hed: Law & Liberty reads a June ruling as a step toward closed primaries
political.insight: Law & Liberty, Thursday: Robert Natelson writes that National Republican Senatorial Committee v. FEC, decided June 30, moved the Supreme Court closer to treating state open-primary laws as a First Amendment problem for parties. Legal argument, not a new holding that bans open primaries.

tech.hed: The Army awarded Palantir $48.1 million to track ammunition
tech.insight: Defense News, Thursday: the Army gave a Palantir subsidiary a $48.1 million contract to build software that consolidates nine legacy ammunition platforms, covering the round from planning through final disposition. The service said Palantir won a three-phase selection over six weeks. Contract, not a fielded system.

tech.hed: Law & Liberty says states are swinging from tax breaks to moratoriums on data centers
tech.insight: Law & Liberty, Thursday: John O. McGinnis writes that states first subsidized data centers for jobs and are now writing special rules, or pauses, once electricity and water demand became unpopular. Argument about equal treatment under law, not a bill count.

tech.hed: Three years of Middle East combat are changing how the Navy fixes ships
tech.insight: USNI News, Wednesday: leaders at a Virginia Beach conference said the conflict with Iran is forcing the Navy to repair and supply ships thousands of miles from logistics hubs, and that long deployments are stacking a maintenance wave at home. Sustainment problem, not a new deployment order.

culture.hed: TruthScript published the third essay on the Christian Sabbath
culture.insight: TruthScript, Wednesday: the third installment of a Presbyterian Polity series, reprinted with permission, continues the biblical case for a Christian Sabbath after the first two parts. Theology essay, not a church-court ruling.
